method.topic_algorithm: TF-IDF + cosine distance + agglomerative average linkage (nearest-neighbor chain)
method.ngram_note: Bigrams join adjacent retained normalized tokens; stopwords have already been removed.
method.clustering_unit: unique whitespace-normalized lowercased fragment; all original occurrences retained
method.sentiment_method: editable phrase/word rules with local negation handling

sentiment_rules.description: Handwritten English phrase and word rules. Scores are rule weights, not probabilities. Validate and extend for your domain.
sentiment_rules.request_pattern: \b(?:i wish|we wish|would like|would prefer|should have|could have|please add|please provide|i want|we want|needs? to be|would be better)\b

rules.pattern: \b(?:would like|would love|should be good|could be good)\b
\b(?:well built|well made|high quality|fuel efficient|easy to use|easy to drive|works well|work well|good support|joy to drive|value for money|attention to detail)\b

\b(?:too hard|too firm|too small|too complicated|too expensive|too noisy|poor support|back pain|broke down|broken down|stopped working|stops working|not user friendly|not user-friendly|does not work|do not work|does not function|do not function|fails to|failed to)\b

method.neutral_policy: Reserved for future explicit neutral annotations; unmatched text is undetermined.
method.review_topic_sentiment_policy: Any positive and negative evidence gives mixed; otherwise known polarity; otherwise undetermined.
method.request_policy: Independent flag; a request is not automatically negative.
method.similarity_note: Cosine similarity is lexical similarity, not a confidence or probability estimate.
method.reproducibility: No random sampling. Same input, parameters, rules and runtime give the same assignments.

warnings: Clusters reflect lexical similarity, not guaranteed semantic topics; human review has not been performed.
Sentiment is a limited English lexicon/rule baseline, not a validated accuracy estimate. No evidence means undetermined, not neutral.
Clause splitting may leave multiple aspects in one fragment or separate a pronoun from its subject.
A fragment receives one cluster. A review can receive several topics through different fragments.
Rare vocabulary removed by min_df and generic statements remain visible as unassigned fragments.
Topic IDs and boundaries may change when the corpus or threshold changes.

reviews.text: Customer wanted to know whether his car includes the remote control parking feature and, if it does, how to operate it. Writer verified that the vehicle is indeed equipped with remote control parking. Writer then called the customer back and walked him through the steps for using it. Writer first confirmed the customer already has the digital key plus configured on his device, and customer answered yes. Writer advised that he should begin the automatic parking process as he normally does by pressing the P button at low speed to bring up the parking cameras, which customer acknowledged. Writer then explained that once parking is activated, he must press the brake, set the parking brake, and follow the on-screen prompt to continue with the maneuver assistant. reviews.text: Customer reported the vehicle has inconsistent scheduled charging, with the car often ignoring the programmed 8:30 PM time slot. Customer noted that sometimes it begins charging immediately after being plugged in even though the settings are not set to charge right away, and at other times it will unexpectedly start charging around 5 PM or 4 PM despite being set for 8:30 PM. Customer stated the system will also change the charging configuration on its own, switching from the time slot setting to charge immediately without any action from the customer. Customer estimated this behavior occurs about half the time, with the other 50 percent working as intended. Customer indicated the issue happens whether charging from roughly 75 percent state of charge to a 90 percent target or at other battery levels, and that it was present both before and after a software update. Customer stated all charging is done at home using a 250 volt outlet in the garage. Customer mentioned the AC limit was originally at 48 amps but later reduced to 32 amps to be cautious, and the problem occurs at both limits. Customer added the outlet is capable of supporting up to 48 amps. Customer advised the vehicle was brought to the dealership, but technicians were unable to duplicate the problem even though the customer provided app screenshots showing the time slot at 8:30 PM while the car charged at 8 PM. Customer said the dealership performed tests and reached out to BMW engineers, but they were unable to resolve the issue. Customer stated the dealership did not reset the software or apply any fix, and engineers concluded there was nothing to be done. Writer suggested the customer continue to observe the charging behavior and contact the dealership again if the problem persists so they can try to reproduce and diagnose it.

Customer stated he is worried about how the range is estimated. Customer stated he drove a 100 mile round trip into the city and back home. Customer stated the car showed roughly 200 miles of range at departure and less than 60 miles remaining once he got back. Customer stated he used efficient mode only for part of the drive home because he began to doubt if there was enough charge to reach his house. Customer stated the average outside temperature was about 32-35 degrees. Customer stated he did not precondition the vehicle before leaving, but the car was kept in his garage overnight. Customer stated the dealership did not clearly explain how to get the best range, and that this is his first electric vehicle.

Writer advised the figure in the instrument cluster is only an estimate. Writer advised that range is affected by climate control usage, driving style, charging behavior, weather, road terrain, and some other variables. Writer advised that preconditioning the vehicle on a cold day will provide a much more accurate range prediction. Writer advised that heating the vehicle up to optimal temperature consumes a lot of battery power, and that not just the cabin but also the battery itself must be warmed to operate efficiently.

Customer stated that if he had the choice, he would change how the auto start-stop works. Customer commented that the system does not feel as smooth as he would like when pulling away, and that he notices the way it turns off and back on. Writer explained that besides turning off the MSA for that drive, there is also an Auto H button located near the start-stop button that the customer should try the next time he is in the car. Writer went over the Auto H, or auto hold, function and described how, when the vehicle is brought to a stop, it will remain stopped even after the driver lifts their foot off the brake pedal, and will only move once the accelerator pedal is pressed. Writer gave the example of sitting at a red light and asked the customer to see whether the car stays stationary or begins to roll ahead when the brake pedal is released before pressing the accelerator. Writer instructed the customer to check for a green light on the Auto H button and stated that a quick press will switch the feature off. Writer clarified that this feature is very useful in stop-and-go traffic, drive-throughs and similar situations where the driver wants to take their foot off the brake while the vehicle remains stopped until the accelerator is used. Writer also noted that auto hold can sometimes lead to slightly jerky movements when parking and suggested this could be playing a role in the smoothness concern the customer mentioned.

i've had the car for about 4 months and i'm splitting my thoughts into pros and cons.

pros:
- driving dynamics: really strong acceleration and power delivery, steering is accurate and easy, the car feels nicely planted in corners, and the steering weight is spot on.
- technology: screens have great clarity and quality, ui is fast, apps and info are solid, speakers/sound system are excellent, the iconic sounds are fun, and the mybmw app integration and features plus the ambient lighting are all big positives.
- styling: love the interior dash design and the look of the front fascia, especially the new lights and the kidney grille.

cons:
- brake pedal feel when slowing down isn't right.
- sound insulation around the b pillars is really weak; tyre/road and other cars' noises are way too loud for a 5 series, so the b pillars on both sides need extra deadening.
- rear legroom should be better for a car this long.
- not enough storage: missing rear seat pockets and nothing under the center console.
- rear lights don't look as iconic as the front, and those two silver bits on the lower bumper just seem out of place.

reviews.text: we swapped a 2021 530 and a 2022 530 for two 2026 530s, and the new cars feel similar in overall quality, ride, and cabin noise. we are still learning our way around the touch screens and the menu structure, and i figure we will get the hang of it over time. i am still trying to convince myself that touch screens are truly as convenient as the old knobs and buttons, since they demand more visual attention instead of simple finger feel. the mapping functions and the heads-up display are better than before, and i really like the route graphics, especially how a real-time camera view pops up when approaching an intersection where you need to turn. nobody was able to tell me why run flat tires are no longer standard equipment. there are two letdowns for me: the removal of the small compartment to the left of the steering wheel, which used to be an ideal spot for sunglasses, and the redesign of the door storage areas into an odd shape, unlike the previous design that could hold an extra drink container. i tried the complimentary feature that lets the car pull itself into a saved parking spot, but i did not feel it was accurate enough to guide the car into my garage without risking contact with the wall on one side or the other vehicle on the opposite side.

reviews.text: Customer stated he has been experiencing connection problems with his iPhone 14 Pro Max on AT&T staying linked to the vehicle when using Apple CarPlay. Customer stated he plans to have his service department investigate the connection issues while the car is in for a recall. Writer advised that there are specific steps to follow that can help improve the connections. Writer advised: 1) Update the phone to the latest iOS, as phone software (iOS 16.6, 16.6.1) has been causing connection problems in the vehicle. 2) Remove the phone from the vehicle's Mobile Devices menu/app. 3) Remove the vehicle from the phone's Bluetooth menu. 4) Go into the CarPlay section in the phone's general settings and tap Forget This Car. 5) Perform a hard reset (force restart) of the iPhone by: a. pressing and quickly releasing the volume up button, b. pressing and quickly releasing the volume down button, c. pressing and holding the side button, d. releasing the side button when the Apple logo appears. 6) Restart the BMW headunit with a telecommunications reboot: a. make sure the engine or motor is turned on, b. press and hold the volume button for 70 seconds, during which the iDrive screen will turn off and on, and c. once the screen turns off the third time, release the volume button. 7) Confirm that phone Wi-Fi is turned on but not connected to another source. 8) Add the device again in the iDrive Mobile Devices menu/app and follow the prompts between the vehicle and phone. 9) Connect to Apple CarPlay when asked. Writer also emailed these instructions to the customer.

reviews.text:
1. i paid extra for the remote parking option, but it often refuses to work. out of 10 attempts it seems to fail about half the time. especially in tight spaces it just won't allow remote parking at all, whether that's because of a sensor error or something else. honestly, i'd like to get my money back for this feature.

2. the body size is bigger than a mercedes-benz e-class or an audi a6, which makes it inconvenient when trying to park or drive through narrow streets. if the body is that large, the cabin should feel more spacious, but the interior doesn't really seem any bigger.

3. the hazard light button is a touch type, so you can't easily tell if it has actually been pressed. when you're in a rush, it's hard to switch it on, which raises the chance of an accident.

4. the bsi engine oil change interval is too long. i'd prefer replacing it every year or at around 15,000 km, but they set it at 20,000 km. trying to save money like that just seems like it will hurt people's impression of how durable the car is.

5. as soon as you approach the vehicle, the side mirrors fold out, which makes it awkward to squeeze between cars in a cramped parking lot. it would be better if the mirrors only opened when the door is actually opened or once the driver gets in.

my first experience with a bmw 7 series was as a passenger back in the early 2000s, and it really left a lasting impression on me. that memory stayed with me and eventually led to buying my first bmw 7 series around 2008. a few years later, i traded that car in for something more suited to family needs, but the feeling of driving a bmw never left. i promised myself i would own another bmw someday.
that time is now, and i'm extremely happy with my 2025 bmw 540i xdrive. the excitement i felt in my early 20s is exactly what i feel again in my early 40s, and even more so. the overall bmw experience is special: the comfort, the ride, the styling, and the distinct personality of the 540i xdrive make it unforgettable.
there are, however, a couple of areas that could be improved. first, the front-facing camera. i get why it's positioned where it is, but aesthetically the placement isn't appealing. from the side, it really sticks out and makes you wonder why it couldn't have been put somewhere more subtle. the bump disrupts the smooth, clean lines of the front bumper. second, the front driver and passenger usb-c charging ports are awkwardly placed. you really have to shift your body noticeably to plug in properly, and a more convenient location would be much better.
all that said, i'm thrilled every time i get behind the wheel of my 540i xdrive and plan to enjoy it for many years.

reviews.text:
after about 20-30 minutes of driving, once i'm over roughly 50 mph, the steering wheel starts feeling choppy as it turns. it's like the power steering isn't matching the wheel movement, and i feel these little "stops" when i move the wheel within maybe 20 degrees of center. i've taken it to my local dealership, but they keep saying they can't reproduce it, even though every time i leave and drive for a while i can bring it back reliably. i reached out to bmw na customer support, and they just say the dealer has to reproduce it.
on longer highway trips this behavior is extremely annoying. small lane adjustments are hard because there's no clear pattern: sometimes the wheel moves smoothly, other times it doesn't. driving with one hand is uncomfortable, and i have to use extra force to turn it, which can lead to over-corrections and even drifting out of the lane. i'm certain it's not the lane assist, since i have that turned off. i've tried different drive modes as well. the car has about 2000 miles now and the issue is still there. i'm honestly at the stage where i'd consider selling a new car if i can't get this fixed. i'd really like to enjoy the car, but this problem makes it impossible for me.

reviews.text: every drive makes me fall for this car all over again. i usually leave it on the charger in my garage and set a departure time so it's preconditioned to the perfect temperature. as i come within about 10 feet with my android phone using digital key plus, the car lights up and unlocks. i love that it powers up without any engine sound, with the seat gliding forward and the steering wheel dropping into place. getting in and out of my tight two-car garage, where my wife's audi sits beside it, is effortless thanks to the overhead view. out on the horrible texas roads, it's insanely quiet and so smooth that i now keep the superb b&w audio turned down much lower than in my old car. even so, it will out-accelerate anything out there with just a gentle press of the accelerator, and the steering reacts instantly with zero roll. it holds the lane and distance to the vehicle ahead, matching its speed calmly while my hands are off the wheel, and the way it does that feels almost uncanny. the eye-controlled lane changes are incredibly convenient, practically like magic. using plug & charge at ea is simple too: plug in, tap the "start charging" button on the display, and go grab a coffee. for me it's the ultimate stress-free and pampering driving experience, in a car that looks better than any of the recent bmws. i only have three small wishes: 1) the eye monitoring is overly picky, since i can't even sip coffee while keeping my eyes on the road above the mug without getting told off by driving assist plus (hands off); 2) the eye-based lane change only works if you're running gps navigation; and 3) in north america the adaptive headlights are just high/low beam instead of the selective dimming used elsewhere, even though selective dimming has been allowed in the us for two years now. i'm also really pleased another ea station opened right along the highway i drive most, roughly midway between home and austin. in my mind the 5-series has always been the best bmw, and this i5 m60 is the best of the 5s. it's pricier, but absolutely 100% worth it.

reviews.text:
overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.
